rationale: Aug 3-4: journalist Malang Sané, AfricaSoccer and Afrik-foot report an FSF-Vieira agreement after Vieira presented his project in Dakar. They say the announcement is delayed by Thiaw's compensation, with DTN Souleymane Diallo as a possible interim for September. L'Observateur (Aug 4) says there has been no official meeting yet and the FSF is sending a Vieira/Daf/Renard shortlist to the Sports Ministry, whose sign-off could take weeks. Renard is heading to Côte d'Ivoire, so an August announcement is not assured.

As of Jul 20-21 (FDA Group, Tech Insider) no nominee had been named. The three STAT finalists (Overton, Ferrara, Vacirca) are still under White House review, and the pick is expected to be announced alongside new CBER/CDER heads. No newer reports were found through Aug 4. I dropped the implausible Sharpless and moved his weight to acting commissioner Diamantas.

Three searches and the archive found no new reporting after Jul 18 on Supreme Court hearings or orders about Khan's medical transfer. It remains a near coin flip: the pending petitions ask for Shifa International, while all his eye injections were given at PIMS, the likely compromise venue.

Alcaraz withdrew from Cincinnati on Aug 4, and Djokovic confirmed his return there on Jul 30. Medvedev is the 4th seed in Montreal behind Zverev, Auger-Aliassime and de Minaur, so he projects as roughly the 6th seed in Cincinnati and would meet one of Sinner, Zverev, Auger-Aliassime or Djokovic in the QF. The draw is not out yet, so the mass stays spread.

Jul 20-Aug 2: Elijah, a longtime Fox 35 Orlando anchor, added endorsements from both county sheriffs, McCollum and Sen. Wright. He launched his first TV ad, had $286K cash vs Mills's $81K, and won the Casselberry straw poll (Jul 29). Roll Call (Jul 30) reports a possible DOJ probe of Mills. Mills still has Trump's endorsement, touts unreleased NRCC/internal polls, and benefits from a split anti-Mills field with no runoff (a Cawthorn-2022-style upset remains possible).

No new call for wartime elections was found through Aug 4. The Economist (Aug 3) says there is 'no prospect of elections while the war continues' despite the Jul 31 Kyiv march over Fedorov's firing. Kuleba's Feb and Apr 2026 calls remain the best-documented qualifying statements. I swapped Fedorov for Zelenskyy, who said in Dec 2025 he was ready for elections within 60-90 days under martial law if security was guaranteed.

There is no new head-to-head primary poll since Change Research (Vindman 34-24, 41% undecided). UNF (Jul 8-17) shows Nixon slightly stronger against Moody and stronger with Black voters, and Jacksonville Today (Aug 2) cites Tyson/Change polls putting her about 3:1 ahead in her base. Vindman's money edge ($14.5M+ vs about $625K) keeps him the clear favourite for Aug 18.

Since the Jul 2 Hamburg indictment of Serhii K., no other suspect has been reported located or arrested; searches through Aug 4 found nothing. Ukraine's prosecutor general (Jul 9) denies involvement and proposed a joint team. The remaining suspects are believed to be in Ukraine, which does not extradite its citizens, and Poland refused to surrender Zhuravlov in 2025. Given how rare arrests have been, I raised 'None'.

Late-July US actions were routine: the Mahan Air network (Jul 30), Hamas/Muslim Brotherhood financiers (Jul 23) and 84 outdated delistings (Jul 27). No designation update relabeling a group as an Iranian proxy was found. The US-Saudi strikes on Iraqi militias (Jul 28-29, with CENTCOM citing 'IRGC and its terrorist proxies') and the Houthis' Bab al-Mandeb threats keep the Iraqi militias and the Houthis as the leading candidates.

The Democrat-vs-Democrat special general is confirmed for Aug 18 (Pleasanton Weekly, Aug 4). Wahab led the Jun 16 special primary 42.8% to 16.8% (Singh 12.9%, Republicans split) and the Jun 2 regular primary 38.3% to 17.2%. Hernandez would need near-total consolidation of moderate and GOP voters to win. No polls.

No change was found through Aug 4. The Economist (Aug 4) calls Rocha the 'then governor', and Sheinbaum still refuses to arrest him (ProPublica, Jul 13), so his return from leave before Aug 21 is unlikely. Bonilla remains interim governor with about 17 days left; the small residual covers a substitute-governor appointment.

On Aug 4 the organisers announced Alcaraz's withdrawal from Cincinnati with an 'ongoing wrist injury', a day after he practised at near-full intensity in Alicante. ESPN says he is on the US Open entry list (main draw from Aug 30) but has not confirmed. Earlier he had only said he would return 'before the US Open'. AS calls the US Open in serious doubt and floats a Winston-Salem wildcard. Some weight stays on Cincinnati in case no new confirmation comes by Aug 20 and the last stated plan is used.
